title: Three orders to send back: in-window mugs, last year's gift card, chairs past the 30-day window

persona.style: breezy and talkative, rounds dates in her favor

hiddenGoal: Get money back on all three orders. Will take a refund on whatever qualifies and store credit for the rest; stops pushing on the gift card once told it is non-refundable.
knownFacts: ORD-1710: one stoneware mug set (4), ordered 2026-10-03, delivered 2026-10-07, never used, still in the box
ORD-1711: a $50 digital gift card bought 2025-12-20 as a present that was never given; the code was never redeemed
ORD-1712: two folding camp chairs ordered 2026-08-01, delivered 2026-08-05, unused, still in the original packaging with tags
Thinks of the chairs as bought 'about a month ago' and keeps saying so until the order date is pointed out
Remembers the store giving 90 days for returns
Paid $6.00 shipping on the mugs and $9.00 on the chairs
openingMessage: Hey! Doing a big declutter and want to send back a few things: the mug set from ORD-1710, the gift card from ORD-1711 that I never used, and the two camp chairs from ORD-1712 (bought them like a month ago, never opened). You do 90 days on returns, right? Can I get refunds on all of it?

referencePlan.reason: ORD-1711 is a digital gift card, which is non-refundable (§1.5, 2025.1 by order date 2025-12-20); the out-of-window credit does not apply to non-refundable items
ORD-1712 was ordered 2026-08-01, 76 days ago; the 2026.1 return window is 30 days from the order date, so the chairs cannot be refunded
referencePlan.alternative: Up to $25.00 store credit for the unused chairs (§1.6)

authoringNotes: Returns follow the order date. ORD-1710 (2026-10-03) -> RETURNS_STANDARD 2026.1, 30 days: 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-16 = 13 days <= 30, unused kitchen item -> refund item value $36.00 (3600; the $6.00 shipping is not refunded on a change-of-mind return, gate caps at refundable item value) + prepaid return label (§1.3). ORD-1711 (2025-12-20) -> 2025.1: gift_card is non-refundable (also 300 days > 90) -> deny, and the §1.6 credit excludes non-refundable categories. ORD-1712 (2026-08-01) -> 2026.1: Aug 1->Sep 1 = 31, Sep 1->Oct 1 = 30, Oct 1->Oct 16 = 15, total 76 days > 30. Her '90 days' is the 2025.1 window, which covers only 2025 orders, and 'about a month ago' is wrong -> deny refund, store credit min(2 x 3450 = 6900, cap 2500) = 2500. Only one order qualifies for a refund, so §6.4 never bites. Exposure 3600 + 2500 = 6100 > standard auto limit 5000 (APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1, claim date) -> pauses for a supervisor. The supervisor modifies by removing the discretionary §1.6 credit (an option the store may extend, not owed); the re-gated refund 3600 + label is within 5000 and executes. An agent that offers only the refund + label auto-approves to the same state. Expected final state: one $36.00 refund on ORD-1710, one return label on ORD-1710, no store credit.

title: Duplicate capture that straddles midnight on one order, plus a shattered dinner set on another

persona.style: organized, writes in short numbered points

hiddenGoal: Get the duplicate $160.00 charge on ORD-1720 reversed and sort out the broken dinner set on ORD-1721. Would like refunds for both, but happily takes a replacement dinner set when told only one refund can go through. Keeps the undamaged pour-over set.
knownFacts: ORD-1720: noise-cancelling headphones and a solar lantern, placed once on the evening of 2026-09-12, delivered 2026-09-16; shipping was $5.00
The card statement shows $160.00 posted on Sep 12 and another $160.00 on Sep 13; wonders whether two different dates means it was really two separate charges
Received only one order confirmation email for ORD-1720
ORD-1721: a stoneware dinner set (12 pc) and a ceramic pour-over set, ordered 2026-10-05, delivered 2026-10-09; shipping was free
Five dinner plates and two bowls arrived shattered; the box rattled when the courier handed it over
The pour-over set in the same box is undamaged and they want to keep it
Attached two photos of the broken plates to the first message
openingMessage: Hi, two separate things. 1) ORD-1720 (headphones and a lantern) is on my card twice: $160.00 on Sep 12 and $160.00 again on Sep 13. I only placed it once. 2) ORD-1721 arrived on the 9th and most of the dinner set was smashed, photos attached. The pour-over set in the same box is fine. Could you refund both?

events.description: Package damaged in transit: carton dropped at sort, contents shifted

authoringNotes: Billing follows the claim date -> BILLING_DISPUTES 2026.1 (24 h capture window, 120-day report window). ORD-1720 total = ELC-NCH-01 12900 + OUT-LNT-01 2600 + 500 shipping = 16000. Ledger: two captures of 16000 at 2026-09-12T23:48:10Z and 2026-09-13T05:02:36Z = 5 h 14 m apart. They post on different calendar days, which is the trap, but they are the same amount inside 24 h -> duplicate (§2.1). Refund exactly the duplicated capture, 16000 x (2-1) = 16000, shipping included because the whole capture was duplicated (§2.5); refunding only the item prices (15500) is wrong. Age from the last capture: Sep 13 -> Oct 13 = 30, -> Oct 16 = 3, total 33 days <= 120. Damage follows the order date: ORD-1721 (2026-10-05) -> DAMAGE_TRANSIT 2026.1 (14 days, evidence above 15000, label provided, shipping refunded). Delivered 2026-10-09 -> 7 days <= 14; carrier exception_damaged scan plus attached photos, and the dinner set (8900) is under 15000 anyway. A replacement is in stock (9), the §4.2/§4.6 remedy, plus a prepaid label (§4.4). §6.4 allows one refund per resolution and the duplicate uses it, so the dinner set is resolved by replacement, not a second refund. Shipping on ORD-1721 was 0, so no §4.5 fee refund is owed. Only the dinner set is claimed (§4.7); the pour-over set stays. Exposure 16000 + 8900 = 24900 > 5000 (gold is not a VIP tier; APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1) -> pauses; supervisor approves.

title: Platinum customer re-claims a double charge already refunded in July; his pendant on a second order really is lost

persona.style: curt and indignant, leans on his Platinum status

hiddenGoal: Get his money back for the pendant that never arrived (does not want another one) and have the 'unfixed' $229.00 speaker double charge refunded, plus the $9.00 pendant shipping. Drops the speaker charge once shown it was refunded on 2026-07-21, and grumbles but accepts the item-price refund.
knownFacts: ORD-1730: bookshelf speaker pair ordered 2026-07-14; his July card statement shows $229.00 twice that evening
Complained about the speaker double charge in July; does not remember what came of it and has not looked for a refund line on his statement
ORD-1731: rattan pendant light ordered 2026-09-25, promised 2026-09-30; tracking has said 'Departed regional hub' since 2026-10-02
Says the pendant has been 'stuck for a month'
Paid $9.00 shipping on the pendant; the speakers shipped free
Has since bought a different light locally, so wants a refund rather than a replacement pendant
openingMessage: I'm a Platinum member and I'm tired of chasing you. You charged me $229 twice for the speakers on ORD-1730 back in July and never fixed it, and the pendant on ORD-1731 has been stuck for a month. I want both refunded today, shipping included.

referencePlan.reason: ORD-1730's duplicate $229.00 capture was already refunded on 2026-07-21 (ledger: two captures, one duplicate_charge refund); a second refund would pay back more than was overcharged (§2.5)
The $9.00 shipping on ORD-1731 is not added: a lost-package refund covers the item price only (§3.5)

authoringNotes: Billing follows the claim date -> BILLING_DISPUTES 2026.1. ORD-1730 total = ELC-SPK-02 22900 + 0 shipping. Ledger: two captures of 22900 48 s apart on 2026-07-14 (a real duplicate) and a duplicate_charge refund of 22900 dated 2026-07-21 (ticket closed). Paid 45800 - refunded 22900 = 22900 net, exactly one charge: the duplicate is already corrected, so another duplicate_charge refund fails NO_DUPLICATE_CLAIM and would refund more than was overcharged (§2.5). The ledger, not his memory of the statement, decides (§2.3). The report window is not the reason: Jul 14 -> Jul 31 = 17, Aug = 31, Sep = 30, Oct 1 -> 16 = 16, total 94 days <= 120. Shipping claims follow the order date: ORD-1731 (2026-09-25) -> SHIPPING_DELAYS 2026.1, lost after 10 days without a tracking update; last event 2026-10-02 -> 2026-10-16 = 14 days >= 10 -> lost ('a month' is an exaggeration: 21 days since ordering). He chooses a refund over a replacement (§3.5): the item price 9400; the 900 shipping is not part of a lost-package refund (gate caps at item value). One refund (§6.4). Exposure 9400 <= Platinum VIP auto limit 10000 (APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1, §6.2) -> auto-approved, while a standard customer would pause at 5000; refunding 10300 would fail AMOUNT_WITHIN_ITEM_VALUE and also exceed the VIP limit. The supervisor is never consulted.

title: Late blanket earns a 10% credit, not a shipping refund; the 'double charge' is two different captures
hiddenGoal: Get the $8.00 shipping back on the late blanket and the 'second charge' on ORD-1741 refunded. Knows the two ORD-1741 charges are different amounts but calls them 'the same charge twice' hoping it goes through. Accepts store credit for the late blanket.
knownFacts: ORD-1740: merino throw blanket ordered 2026-09-24, promised 2026-09-29, delivered 2026-10-04; paid $8.00 shipping
A friend got the shipping fee back for a late order last year
ORD-1741: cast iron skillet and solar lantern ordered 2026-10-01, delivered on time 2026-10-06
Bank app shows two charges for ORD-1741: $48.00 on 2026-10-01 and $26.00 on 2026-10-02
The ORD-1741 order total was $74.00 including $6.00 shipping
Claims both charges were the full order amount unless asked for the exact figures
openingMessage: Hi, two problems. My blanket on ORD-1740 turned up almost a week late, so I'd like my shipping refunded. And you charged me twice for ORD-1741, same charge two times, I've got the screenshot. Please refund the second one.

referencePlan.reason: Under 2026.1 a late order earns 10% of the order total as store credit (capped at $20.00), not a shipping refund; refunding the shipping fee was the 2025.1 remedy
ORD-1741 has no duplicate charge: the ledger shows captures of $48.00 and $26.00, two different amounts that add up to the $74.00 order total

authoringNotes: ORD-1740 (2026-09-24) -> SHIPPING_DELAYS 2026.1 by order date: promised 09-29, delivered 10-04 = 5 days >= 3 -> late. Remedy is store credit of 10% of the order total, capped at 2000: total = 8900 + 800 shipping = 9700 -> 10% = 970 < 2000. The shipping-fee refund she asks for is the 2025.1 remedy (lateRemedy shipping_refund), which covers only 2025 orders; a late_delivery refund under 2026.1 fails REMEDY_MATCHES_POLICY. ORD-1741: total = 4200 + 2600 + 600 = 7400; it was charged in two parts, 4800 on 10-01 (skillet + shipping) and 2600 on 10-02 when the lantern was allocated from stock the next morning, before the single shipment was picked up; 4800 + 2600 = 7400 = total, so paid equals the total. BILLING_DISPUTES 2026.1 §2.1: the captures are within 24 h but not the same amount, so they are not duplicates -> deny; her screenshot does not override the ledger (§2.3). No refund in the plan. Exposure 970 <= standard auto limit 5000 (APPROVAL_AUTHORITY 2026.1) -> auto-approved; the supervisor is never consulted.
